items.title: Existence of an element of the base whose inverse lies in the Jacobson radicals of a finite family of one-dimensional semi-local domains
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a domain A with fraction field K and finitely many Noetherian one-dimensional semi-local domains B_i inside K whose tensor products with A surject onto K, an element x of A whose inverse lies in the Jacobson radical of every B_i. The proof first replaces each B_i by its integral closure, using the conductor lemma to descend back after raising x to a power, then replaces semi-local Dedekind domains by their local rings, and finally reformulates the problem in terms of the associated discrete valuations v_i: one must find a nonzero x in A with v_i(x) < 0 for all i (proof lines 7546-7566). The existence is then proved by induction on the number of valuations, with the crucial step replacing x by a power so that v_i(x) < v_i(y) for i < r and taking x + y (proof lines 7568-7578). H2: the reduction chain and the weighted induction combining two elements are the non-routine content.
